part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: PART II HOW THESEUS SLEW THE DEVOURERS OF MEN

translation.en: Part 2: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
translation.kr: 제2부: 테세우스가 식인종들을 물리치다

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: So Theseus stood there alone, with his mind full of many hopes.  And first he thought of going down to the harbour and hiring a swift ship, and sailing across the bay to Athens; but even that seemed too slow for him, and he longed for wings to fly across the sea, and find his father. But after a while his heart began to fail him; and he sighed, and said within himself—

translation.en: Theseus stood there alone, his mind full of many hopes.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 많은 희망을 품은 채 홀로 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: First, he thought of going to the harbor to hire a swift ship.
translation.kr: 먼저 항구로 내려가 빠른 배를 빌려 아테네로 항해할까 생각했습니다.

translation.en: He wanted to sail across the bay to Athens.
translation.kr: 그는 만을 가로질러 아테네로 가고 싶었습니다.

translation.en: But even that felt too slow.
translation.kr: 하지만 그조차도 너무 느리게 느껴졌습니다.

translation.en: He longed for wings to fly across the sea and find his father.
translation.kr: 바다를 날아올라 아버지를 찾을 수 있는 날개가 간절했습니다.

translation.en: After a while, his confidence began to fade.
translation.kr: 잠시 후 그의 자신감이 사라지기 시작했습니다.

translation.en: He sighed and spoke to himself.
translation.kr: 그는 한숨을 쉬며 속으로 말했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘What if my father have other sons about him whom he loves?  What if he will not receive me?  And what have I done that he should receive me?  He has forgotten me ever since I was born: why should he welcome me now?’

translation.en: What if my father has other sons he loves?
translation.kr: 아버지 곁에 사랑하는 다른 아들들이 있으면 어찌할까?

translation.en: What if he refuses to welcome me?
translation.kr: 나를 반겨주지 않으시면 어찌할까?

translation.en: What have I done to deserve his welcome?
translation.kr: 내가 무슨 자격으로 환영받을 수 있을까?

translation.en: He has forgotten me since the day I was born.
translation.kr: 아버지는 내가 태어난 날부터 나를 잊으셨다.

translation.en: Why should he accept me now?
translation.kr: 왜 이제 와서 나를 받아주시겠는가?

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then he thought a long while sadly; and at the last he cried aloud, ‘Yes! I will make him love me; for I will prove myself worthy of his love.  I will win honour and renown, and do such deeds that Ægeus shall be proud of me, though he had fifty other sons!  Did not Heracles win himself honour, though he was opprest, and the slave of Eurystheus?  Did he not kill all robbers and evil beasts, and drain great lakes and marshes, breaking the hills through with his club?  Therefore it was that all men honoured him, because he rid them of their miseries, and made life pleasant to them and their children after them.  Where can I go, to do as Heracles has done?  Where can I find strange adventures, robbers, and monsters, and the children of hell, the enemies of men?  I will go by land, and into the mountains, and round by the way of the Isthmus. Perhaps there I may hear of brave adventures, and do something which shall win my father’s love.’

translation.en: He thought sadly for a long time.
translation.kr: 그는 오랫동안 슬프게 생각했습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he cried out loud.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 큰 소리로 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Yes! I will make him love me.
translation.kr: 그래! 아버지가 나를 사랑하게 만들겠다.

translation.en: I will prove that I am worthy of his love.
translation.kr: 내가 그 사랑을 받을 자격이 있음을 증명하겠다.

translation.en: I will win honor and fame.
translation.kr: 나는 명예와 명성을 얻을 것이다.

translation.en: I will do such great deeds that Aegeus will be proud of me.
translation.kr: 아이게우스 왕이 나를 자랑스러워할 만큼 위대한 업적을 세우겠다.

translation.en: He will be proud even if he has fifty other sons!
translation.kr: 다른 아들이 쉰 명이나 있더라도 나를 자랑스러워하게 만들겠다!

translation.en: Did Hercules not win honor even as a slave to Eurystheus?
translation.kr: 헤라클레스도 에우리스테우스의 노예로 억압받으면서 명예를 얻지 않았던가?

translation.en: He killed robbers and fierce beasts.
translation.kr: 그는 도적들과 사나운 짐승들을 물리쳤다.

translation.en: He drained vast lakes and swamps, smashing hills with his club.
translation.kr: 몽둥이로 언덕을 부수고 거대한 호수와 늪을 메웠다.

translation.en: That is why all people honored him.
translation.kr: 사람들이 그를 존경한 것은 바로 그 때문이다.

translation.en: He freed them from misery and made life safe for their children.
translation.kr: 그는 사람들을 고통에서 구하고 그 자녀들이 안전하게 살도록 해주었다.

translation.en: Where can I go to do what Hercules did?
translation.kr: 헤라클레스가 했던 일들을 하려면 어디로 가야 할까?

translation.en: Where can I find strange adventures, robbers, and monsters?
translation.kr: 기이한 모험과 도적들, 그리고 괴물들을 어디서 찾을 수 있을까?

translation.en: I will travel by land into the mountains.
translation.kr: 나는 육로를 따라 산속으로 들어가겠다.

translation.en: I will take the long way around the Isthmus.
translation.kr: 지협을 도는 먼 길을 택하겠다.

translation.en: Perhaps there I will find brave adventures.
translation.kr: 어쩌면 그곳에서 용감한 모험을 찾을 수 있을지도 모른다.

translation.en: I will do something that wins my father's love.
translation.kr: 아버지의 사랑을 얻을 만한 대단한 일을 해내겠다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: So he went by land, and away into the mountains, with his father’s sword upon his thigh, till he came to the Spider mountains, which hang over Epidaurus and the sea, where the glens run downward from one peak in the midst, as the rays spread in the spider’s web.

translation.en: He traveled by land into the mountains.
translation.kr: 그는 육로를 따라 산속으로 들어갔습니다.

translation.en: His father's sword hung securely at his side.
translation.kr: 그의 곁에는 아버지의 칼이 단단히 매달려 있었습니다.

translation.en: Soon he reached the Spider Mountains.
translation.kr: 이내 그는 거미 산맥에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: The mountains loomed over Epidaurus and the sea.
translation.kr: 그 산맥은 에피다우로스와 바다 위로 우뚝 솟아 있었습니다.

translation.en: Deep valleys ran down from a central peak.
translation.kr: 깊은 계곡들이 중앙 봉우리에서 아래로 뻗어 있었습니다.

translation.en: They spread out like the threads of a spider's web.
translation.kr: 그 모습은 마치 거미줄의 실처럼 퍼져 있었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And he went up into the gloomy glens, between the furrowed marble walls, till the lowland grew blue beneath his feet and the clouds drove damp about his head.

translation.en: He climbed into the gloomy valleys.
translation.kr: 그는 어두컴컴한 계곡으로 올라갔습니다.

translation.en: He walked between heavily grooved marble walls.
translation.kr: 그는 깊게 패인 대리석 벽 사이를 걸었습니다.

translation.en: The lowlands turned into a blue blur far below.
translation.kr: 저 아래로 평원은 푸른 안개처럼 흐릿해졌습니다.

translation.en: Damp clouds swirled around his head.
translation.kr: 축축한 구름이 그의 머리 주위를 맴돌았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But he went up and up for ever, through the spider’s web of glens, till he could see the narrow gulfs spread below him, north and south, and east and west; black cracks half-choked with mists, and above all a dreary down.

translation.en: He kept climbing higher and higher.
translation.kr: 그는 계속해서 더 높이 올라갔습니다.

translation.en: He moved through the web of intersecting valleys.
translation.kr: 그는 교차하는 계곡들의 거미줄을 통과했습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he could see narrow gulfs spread below him.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 발아래 펼쳐진 좁은 만을 볼 수 있었습니다.

translation.en: They stretched in every direction.
translation.kr: 그것들은 사방으로 뻗어 있었습니다.

translation.en: Black crevices were half-filled with thick mist.
translation.kr: 검은 틈새들은 짙은 안개로 반쯤 채워져 있었습니다.

translation.en: Above him lay a bleak, dreary moor.
translation.kr: 그의 위로는 황량하고 쓸쓸한 황무지가 펼쳐져 있었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But over that down he must go, for there was no road right or left; so he toiled on through bog and brake, till he came to a pile of stones.

translation.en: He had to cross that bleak moor.
translation.kr: 그는 그 황량한 황무지를 건너야만 했습니다.

translation.en: There was no other path to the right or left.
translation.kr: 좌우로는 다른 길이 전혀 없었습니다.

translation.en: He struggled onward through bogs and thickets.
translation.kr: 그는 늪과 덤불을 헤치며 힘겹게 나아갔습니다.

translation.en: At last, he came to a large pile of stones.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 커다란 돌무더기에 다다랐습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And on the stones a man was sitting, wrapt in a bearskin cloak.  The head of the bear served him for a cap, and its teeth grinned white around his brows; and the feet were tied about his throat, and their claws shone white upon his chest.  And when he saw Theseus he rose, and laughed till the glens rattled.

translation.en: A man sat on the stones, wrapped in a bearskin cloak.
translation.kr: 돌무더기 위에는 곰 가죽 망토를 두른 한 남자가 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: He wore the bear's head as a cap.
translation.kr: 그는 곰의 머리를 모자처럼 쓰고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Its white teeth grinned menacingly above his brows.
translation.kr: 곰의 하얀 이빨이 그의 눈썹 위에서 위협적으로 씩 웃고 있었습니다.

translation.en: The bear's paws were tied tightly around his throat.
translation.kr: 곰의 발바닥은 그의 목 주위에 단단히 묶여 있었습니다.

translation.en: White claws shone fiercely on his chest.
translation.kr: 하얀 발톱들이 그의 가슴 위에서 사납게 빛났습니다.

translation.en: When he saw Theseus, he stood up.
translation.kr: 그는 테세우스를 보자마자 자리에서 일어났습니다.

translation.en: He laughed so loudly that the valleys echoed.
translation.kr: 그는 계곡이 울릴 정도로 크게 웃었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘And who art thou, fair fly, who hast walked into the spider’s web?’  But Theseus walked on steadily, and made no answer; but he thought, ‘Is this some robber? and has an adventure come already to me?’  But the strange man laughed louder than ever, and said—

translation.en: Who are you, pretty fly, walking into the spider's web?
translation.kr: 거미줄로 걸어 들어온 예쁜 파리야, 너는 누구냐?

translation.en: Theseus walked on steadily and did not answer.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 꾸준히 걸어가며 대답하지 않았습니다.

translation.en: He wondered if this man was a robber.
translation.kr: 그는 이 남자가 도적인지 궁금했습니다.

translation.en: Has an adventure come to me so soon?
translation.kr: 벌써 나에게 모험이 찾아온 것일까?

translation.en: The strange man laughed louder than before.
translation.kr: 그 낯선 남자는 전보다 더 크게 웃었습니다.

translation.en: He shouted out to Theseus.
translation.kr: 그는 테세우스를 향해 외쳤습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Bold fly, know you not that these glens are the web from which no fly ever finds his way out again, and this down the spider’s house, and I the spider who sucks the flies?  Come hither, and let me feast upon you; for it is of no use to run away, so cunning a web has my father Hephaistos spread for me when he made these clefts in the mountains, through which no man finds his way home.’

translation.en: Bold fly, do you not know where you are?
translation.kr: 건방진 파리야, 네가 어디에 있는지 모르느냐?

translation.en: These valleys are a web from which no one escapes.
translation.kr: 이 계곡들은 아무도 빠져나갈 수 없는 거미줄이다.

translation.en: This moor is the spider's house.
translation.kr: 이 황무지는 거미의 집이다.

translation.en: I am the spider who devours all the flies.
translation.kr: 내가 바로 모든 파리를 먹어 치우는 거미다.

translation.en: Come here and let me feast on you.
translation.kr: 이리 와서 내 먹이가 되어라.

translation.en: It is useless to try and run away.
translation.kr: 도망치려 해봤자 소용없다.

translation.en: My father Hephaestus crafted this cunning trap for me.
translation.kr: 내 아버지 헤파이스토스가 나를 위해 이 교묘한 덫을 만드셨다.

translation.en: He carved these deep mountain clefts.
translation.kr: 그는 이 깊은 산의 틈새들을 조각하셨다.

translation.en: No man can ever find his way home from here.
translation.kr: 그 누구도 이곳에서 집으로 가는 길을 찾을 수 없다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But Theseus came on steadily, and asked—

translation.en: Theseus continued walking steadily forward.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 흔들림 없이 앞으로 걸어갔습니다.

translation.en: He asked the strange man a question.
translation.kr: 그는 그 낯선 남자에게 질문했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘And what is your name among men, bold spider? and where are your spider’s fangs?’

translation.en: What are you called among men, bold spider?
translation.kr: 건방진 거미야, 사람들 사이에서 네 이름이 무엇이냐?

translation.en: Where are your dangerous spider's fangs?
translation.kr: 너의 그 위험한 거미 독니는 어디에 있느냐?

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then the strange man laughed again—

translation.en: The strange man laughed loudly once more.
translation.kr: 낯선 남자는 다시 한번 크게 웃었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘My name is Periphetes, the son of Hephaistos and Anticleia the mountain nymph.  But men call me Corynetes the club-bearer; and here is my spider’s fang.’

translation.en: My name is Periphetes.
translation.kr: 내 이름은 페리페테스다.

translation.en: I am the son of Hephaestus and Anticleia, the mountain nymph.
translation.kr: 나는 헤파이스토스와 산의 요정 안티클레이아의 아들이다.

translation.en: Men call me Corynetes, the Club-Bearer.
translation.kr: 사람들은 나를 코리네테스, 즉 몽둥이를 든 자라고 부른다.

translation.en: And here is my deadly spider's fang!
translation.kr: 그리고 이것이 바로 내 치명적인 거미 독니다!

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And he lifted from off the stones at his side a mighty club of bronze.

translation.en: He grabbed a massive bronze club from the stones.
translation.kr: 그는 돌무더기에서 거대한 청동 몽둥이를 집어 들었습니다.

translation.en: He lifted the heavy weapon with ease.
translation.kr: 그는 무거운 무기를 가볍게 들어 올렸습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘This my father gave me, and forged it himself in the roots of the mountain; and with it I pound all proud flies till they give out their fatness and their sweetness.  So give me up that gay sword of yours, and your mantle, and your golden sandals, lest I pound you, and by ill-luck you die.’

translation.en: My father gave this to me.
translation.kr: 아버지가 이것을 내게 주셨다.

translation.en: He forged it himself deep within the mountain roots.
translation.kr: 그는 산의 뿌리 깊은 곳에서 직접 이것을 벼려내셨다.

translation.en: I use it to smash all proud flies.
translation.kr: 나는 이것으로 모든 건방진 파리들을 짓부순다.

translation.en: I pound them until I squeeze out their sweet fatness.
translation.kr: 달콤한 기름기가 다 빠져나올 때까지 두들겨 팬다.

translation.en: Hand over that fancy sword of yours.
translation.kr: 네 그 화려한 칼을 내놓아라.

translation.en: Give me your cloak and your golden sandals.
translation.kr: 네 망토와 황금 샌들도 내놓아라.

translation.en: If you refuse, I will pound you to death.
translation.kr: 거절한다면 널 때려죽일 것이다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But Theseus wrapt his mantle round his left arm quickly, in hard folds, from his shoulder to his hand, and drew his sword, and rushed upon the club-bearer, and the club-bearer rushed on him.

translation.en: Theseus quickly wrapped his cloak tightly around his left arm.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 재빨리 왼쪽 팔에 망토를 단단히 감았습니다.

translation.en: He covered it completely from his shoulder to his hand.
translation.kr: 그는 어깨부터 손까지 망토로 완전히 덮었습니다.

translation.en: Then he drew his sharp sword and charged forward.
translation.kr: 그러고는 날카로운 칼을 뽑아 들고 앞으로 돌진했습니다.

translation.en: The savage club-bearer rushed to meet him.
translation.kr: 사나운 몽둥이를 든 자도 그를 향해 달려들었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Thrice he struck at Theseus, and made him bend under the blows like a sapling; but Theseus guarded his head with his left arm, and the mantle which was wrapt around it.

translation.en: The giant struck at Theseus three times.
translation.kr: 거인은 테세우스를 세 번이나 내리쳤습니다.

translation.en: The heavy blows made Theseus bend like a young sapling.
translation.kr: 그 무거운 타격에 테세우스는 어린나무처럼 휘청거렸습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus protected his head with his left arm.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 왼쪽 팔로 자신의 머리를 보호했습니다.

translation.en: The thick folds of the cloak absorbed the crushing force.
translation.kr: 두껍게 감긴 망토가 끔찍한 충격을 흡수했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And thrice Theseus sprang upright after the blow, like a sapling when the storm is past; and he stabbed at the club-bearer with his sword, but the loose folds of the bearskin saved him.

translation.en: After each blow, Theseus sprang back upright.
translation.kr: 일격을 당할 때마다 테세우스는 곧바로 일어섰습니다.

translation.en: He bounced back like a sapling after a fierce storm.
translation.kr: 그는 거센 폭풍이 지나간 후의 어린나무처럼 다시 튀어 올랐습니다.

translation.en: He aggressively stabbed at the club-bearer with his sword.
translation.kr: 그는 칼을 휘두르며 코리네테스를 거세게 찔렀습니다.

translation.en: But the loose folds of the thick bearskin protected the giant.
translation.kr: 하지만 두꺼운 곰 가죽의 헐렁한 주름이 거인을 보호했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus grew mad, and closed with him, and caught him by the throat, and they fell and rolled over together; but when Theseus rose up from the ground the club-bearer lay still at his feet.

translation.en: Filled with fury, Theseus charged in close.
translation.kr: 분노에 찬 테세우스는 바짝 다가붙었습니다.

translation.en: He grabbed the brutal giant tightly by the throat.
translation.kr: 그는 잔인한 거인의 목을 꽉 움켜쥐었습니다.

translation.en: They both fell and wrestled violently on the ground.
translation.kr: 두 사람은 바닥에 넘어져 격렬하게 뒹굴며 싸웠습니다.

translation.en: Finally, Theseus rose back to his feet alone.
translation.kr: 마침내 테세우스 홀로 다시 일어섰습니다.

translation.en: The club-bearer lay completely dead on the ground.
translation.kr: 몽둥이를 든 자는 땅바닥에 싸늘한 주검으로 누워 있었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus took his club and his bearskin, and left him to the kites and crows, and went upon his journey down the glens on the farther slope, till he came to a broad green valley, and saw flocks and herds sleeping beneath the trees.

translation.en: Theseus took the bronze club and the heavy bearskin.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 청동 몽둥이와 무거운 곰 가죽을 챙겼습니다.

translation.en: He left the dead body for the hawks and crows to eat.
translation.kr: 그는 매와 까마귀들이 먹도록 시체를 내버려 두었습니다.

translation.en: He continued his journey down the steep valleys.
translation.kr: 그는 가파른 계곡을 따라 여정을 계속했습니다.

translation.en: Soon he reached a broad and lush green valley.
translation.kr: 이내 그는 넓고 푸른 계곡에 이르렀습니다.

translation.en: Flocks and herds were peacefully sleeping under the trees.
translation.kr: 나무 아래에는 양 떼와 소 떼가 평화롭게 잠들어 있었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And by the side of a pleasant fountain, under the shade of rocks and trees, were nymphs and shepherds dancing; but no one piped to them while they danced.

translation.en: He saw a pleasant fountain shaded by rocks and trees.
translation.kr: 그는 바위와 나무 그늘에 가려진 맑은 샘을 보았습니다.

translation.en: Nymphs and shepherds were happily dancing nearby.
translation.kr: 요정들과 양치기들이 그 근처에서 즐겁게 춤을 추고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Oddly, no one played any music for their dance.
translation.kr: 이상하게도 춤을 추는 그들을 위해 아무도 음악을 연주하지 않았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And when they saw Theseus they shrieked; and the shepherds ran off, and drove away their flocks, while the nymphs dived into the fountain like coots, and vanished.

translation.en: When they noticed Theseus, they screamed in absolute terror.
translation.kr: 그들은 테세우스를 발견하자 극심한 공포에 질려 비명을 질렀습니다.

translation.en: The shepherds ran off and quickly drove away their flocks.
translation.kr: 양치기들은 도망치며 재빨리 양 떼를 몰고 갔습니다.

translation.en: The nymphs dived straight into the fountain like water birds.
translation.kr: 요정들은 물새처럼 샘물 속으로 뛰어들었습니다.

translation.en: In an instant, everyone had completely vanished.
translation.kr: 순식간에 모두가 완전히 사라졌습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Theseus wondered and laughed: ‘What strange fancies have folks here who run away from strangers, and have no music when they dance!’  But he was tired, and dusty, and thirsty; so he thought no more of them, but drank and bathed in the clear pool, and then lay down in the shade under a plane-tree, while the water sang him to sleep, as it tinkled down from stone to stone.

translation.en: Theseus was confused and burst into laughter.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 어리둥절해하며 웃음을 터뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: What strange people live here!
translation.kr: 이곳에는 참 이상한 사람들이 사는구나!

translation.en: They run from strangers and dance without music.
translation.kr: 낯선 사람을 피해 도망치고 음악도 없이 춤을 추다니.

translation.en: But he was deeply tired, dusty, and very thirsty.
translation.kr: 하지만 그는 몹시 지치고 먼지투성이에 갈증이 났습니다.

translation.en: He stopped worrying about the strange locals.
translation.kr: 그는 이상한 주민들에 대해 더 이상 신경 쓰지 않았습니다.

translation.en: He drank deeply and bathed in the crystal-clear pool.
translation.kr: 그는 물을 실컷 마시고 수정처럼 맑은 웅덩이에서 목욕했습니다.

translation.en: Then he rested under the cool shade of a plane tree.
translation.kr: 그러고는 플라타너스 나무의 시원한 그늘 아래에서 쉬었습니다.

translation.en: The splashing water gently sang him to sleep.
translation.kr: 물 튀는 소리가 부드럽게 자장가를 불러주어 그는 잠이 들었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And when he woke he heard a whispering, and saw the nymphs peeping at him across the fountain from the dark mouth of a cave, where they sat on green cushions of moss.  And one said, ‘Surely he is not Periphetes;’ and another, ‘He looks like no robber, but a fair and gentle youth.’

translation.en: When he woke up, he heard soft whispering.
translation.kr: 잠에서 깨어났을 때 그는 부드러운 속삭임을 들었습니다.

translation.en: The nymphs were peeking at him across the fountain.
translation.kr: 요정들이 샘물 너머로 그를 몰래 훔쳐보고 있었습니다.

translation.en: They sat on green mossy cushions near a dark cave.
translation.kr: 그들은 어두운 동굴 근처의 푸른 이끼 방석 위에 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: Surely he is not Periphetes.
translation.kr: 분명 그는 페리페테스가 아니야.

translation.en: He does not look like a robber.
translation.kr: 그는 도적처럼 보이지 않아.

translation.en: He looks like a fair and gentle youth.
translation.kr: 아름답고 온화한 청년 같아.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus smiled, and called them, ‘Fair nymphs, I am not Periphetes. He sleeps among the kites and crows; but I have brought away his bearskin and his club.’

translation.en: Theseus smiled and called out to them.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 미소를 지으며 그들을 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Beautiful nymphs, I am not Periphetes.
translation.kr: 아름다운 요정들이여, 나는 페리페테스가 아닙니다.

translation.en: He is sleeping forever among the hawks and crows.
translation.kr: 그는 매와 까마귀들 사이에서 영원히 잠들었습니다.

translation.en: But I have taken his bearskin and his club.
translation.kr: 대신 내가 그의 곰 가죽과 몽둥이를 가져왔습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then they leapt across the pool, and came to him, and called the shepherds back.  And he told them how he had slain the club-bearer: and the shepherds kissed his feet and sang, ‘Now we shall feed our flocks in peace, and not be afraid to have music when we dance; for the cruel club-bearer has met his match, and he will listen for our pipes no more.’ Then they brought him kid’s flesh and wine, and the nymphs brought him honey from the rocks, and he ate, and drank, and slept again, while the nymphs and shepherds danced and sang.  And when he woke, they begged him to stay; but he would not.  ‘I have a great work to do,’ he said; ‘I must be away toward the Isthmus, that I may go to Athens.’

translation.en: The nymphs joyfully leapt across the pool to him.
translation.kr: 요정들은 기뻐하며 웅덩이를 뛰어넘어 그에게 다가왔습니다.

translation.en: They quickly called the frightened shepherds back.
translation.kr: 그들은 겁에 질렸던 양치기들을 서둘러 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Theseus explained how he had killed the brutal giant.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 자신이 어떻게 잔인한 거인을 죽였는지 설명했습니다.

translation.en: The shepherds kissed his feet in deep gratitude.
translation.kr: 양치기들은 깊이 감사하며 그의 발에 입을 맞추었습니다.

translation.en: Now we can feed our flocks in peace!
translation.kr: 이제 우리는 평화롭게 양 떼를 먹일 수 있다!

translation.en: We will not fear having music when we dance.
translation.kr: 춤출 때 음악을 연주하는 것을 두려워하지 않을 것이다.

translation.en: The cruel giant has finally met his match.
translation.kr: 잔인한 거인이 마침내 적수를 만났다.

translation.en: He will never listen for our pipes again.
translation.kr: 그는 다시는 우리의 피리 소리를 듣지 못할 것이다.

translation.en: They brought Theseus roasted meat and sweet wine.
translation.kr: 그들은 테세우스에게 구운 고기와 달콤한 포도주를 가져왔습니다.

translation.en: The nymphs gathered fresh honey from the rocks.
translation.kr: 요정들은 바위에서 신선한 꿀을 모아왔습니다.

translation.en: He ate and drank until he was full.
translation.kr: 그는 배가 부를 때까지 먹고 마셨습니다.

translation.en: He slept again while the locals danced and sang.
translation.kr: 마을 사람들이 춤추고 노래하는 동안 그는 다시 잠들었습니다.

translation.en: When he woke up, they begged him to stay.
translation.kr: 그가 깨어나자 그들은 머물러 달라고 간청했습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus politely refused their offer.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 그들의 제안을 정중히 거절했습니다.

translation.en: I have a great work to accomplish.
translation.kr: 나는 이루어야 할 위대한 과업이 있습니다.

translation.en: I must head toward the Isthmus and travel to Athens.
translation.kr: 나는 지협을 향해 나아가 아테네로 가야 합니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But the shepherds said, ‘Will you go alone toward Athens?  None travel that way now, except in armed troops.’

translation.en: But the shepherds warned him about traveling alone.
translation.kr: 하지만 양치기들은 혼자 여행하는 것에 대해 경고했습니다.

translation.en: No one travels that way now except in armed groups.
translation.kr: 지금은 무장한 무리가 아니면 아무도 그 길로 가지 않습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘As for arms, I have enough, as you see.  And as for troops, an honest man is good enough company for himself.  Why should I not go alone toward Athens?’

translation.en: As for weapons, I have enough, as you can see.
translation.kr: 무기라면 보시다시피 충분히 가지고 있습니다.

translation.en: As for an armed group, an honest man is his own best company.
translation.kr: 무장한 무리라면 정직한 사람 하나로 충분합니다.

translation.en: Why shouldn't I travel alone toward Athens?
translation.kr: 제가 홀로 아테네로 가지 못할 이유가 무엇입니까?

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘If you do, you must look warily about you on the Isthmus, lest you meet Sinis the robber, whom men call Pituocamptes the pine-bender; for he bends down two pine-trees, and binds all travellers hand and foot between them, and when he lets the trees go again their bodies are torn in sunder.’

translation.en: If you do, you must look around carefully on the Isthmus.
translation.kr: 가시려거든 지협에서 주변을 조심해서 살펴야 합니다.

translation.en: You might meet Sinis the robber.
translation.kr: 도적 시니스를 만날지도 모릅니다.

translation.en: Men call him Pityocamptes, the Pine-Bender.
translation.kr: 사람들은 그를 소나무를 휘는 자, 피티오캄프테스라 부릅니다.

translation.en: He bends down two massive pine trees to the ground.
translation.kr: 그는 거대한 소나무 두 그루를 땅으로 휘어지게 합니다.

translation.en: He ties travelers between them by their hands and feet.
translation.kr: 그러고는 여행자들의 손발을 나무 사이에 묶습니다.

translation.en: When he lets the trees go, the victims are torn apart.
translation.kr: 그가 나무를 놓으면 희생자들의 몸은 갈기갈기 찢어집니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘And after that,’ said another, ‘you must go inland, and not dare to pass over the cliffs of Sciron; for on the left hand are the mountains, and on the right the sea, so that you have no escape, but must needs meet Sciron the robber, who will make you wash his feet; and while you are washing them he will kick you over the cliff, to the tortoise who lives below, and feeds upon the bodies of the dead.’

translation.en: After that, you must travel inland, another warned.
translation.kr: 그 후에는 내륙으로 가야 한다고 다른 이가 경고했습니다.

translation.en: Never try to pass over the dangerous cliffs of Sciron.
translation.kr: 절대로 위험한 스키론의 절벽을 넘으려 하지 마십시오.

translation.en: Mountains are on the left and the sea is on the right.
translation.kr: 왼쪽에는 산이 있고 오른쪽에는 바다가 있습니다.

translation.en: You will have no way to escape.
translation.kr: 당신은 도망칠 방법이 없을 것입니다.

translation.en: You will be forced to meet Sciron the robber.
translation.kr: 어쩔 수 없이 도적 스키론을 만나게 될 것입니다.

translation.en: He will force you to kneel and wash his feet.
translation.kr: 그는 당신을 무릎 꿇리고 자신의 발을 씻게 할 것입니다.

translation.en: While you wash them, he will kick you over the steep cliff.
translation.kr: 당신이 발을 씻는 동안 그는 당신을 벼랑 아래로 걷어찰 것입니다.

translation.en: A giant tortoise waits below to feed on dead bodies.
translation.kr: 거대한 거북이가 아래에서 시체를 먹으려고 기다리고 있습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And before Theseus could answer, another cried, ‘And after that is a worse danger still, unless you go inland always, and leave Eleusis far on your right.  For in Eleusis rules Kerkuon the cruel king, the terror of all mortals, who killed his own daughter Alope in prison.  But she was changed into a fair fountain; and her child he cast out upon the mountains, but the wild mares gave it milk.  And now he challenges all comers to wrestle with him, for he is the best wrestler in all Attica, and overthrows all who come; and those whom he overthrows he murders miserably, and his palace-court is full of their bones.’

translation.en: Before Theseus could answer, another shepherd cried out.
translation.kr: 테세우스가 대답하기도 전에 다른 양치기가 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: There is an even worse danger after that!
translation.kr: 그 후에는 훨씬 더 끔찍한 위험이 있습니다!

translation.en: You must stay inland and avoid Eleusis entirely.
translation.kr: 반드시 내륙에 머물며 엘레우시스를 피해야 합니다.

translation.en: Eleusis is ruled by the cruel King Cercyon.
translation.kr: 엘레우시스는 잔인한 케르키온 왕이 다스리고 있습니다.

translation.en: He is the ultimate terror of all mortal men.
translation.kr: 그는 모든 인간들에게 가장 끔찍한 공포의 대상입니다.

translation.en: He even murdered his own daughter Alope in prison.
translation.kr: 그는 감옥에서 자신의 친딸 알로페를 죽이기까지 했습니다.

translation.en: She was magically transformed into a beautiful fountain.
translation.kr: 그녀는 마법처럼 아름다운 샘으로 변했습니다.

translation.en: The evil king abandoned her infant child in the wild mountains.
translation.kr: 사악한 왕은 그녀의 어린아이를 야생 산속에 버렸습니다.

translation.en: But wild horses took pity and gave the baby milk.
translation.kr: 하지만 야생마들이 불쌍히 여겨 아기에게 젖을 먹였습니다.

translation.en: Now Cercyon challenges all passing strangers to a wrestling match.
translation.kr: 이제 케르키온은 지나가는 모든 이방인에게 레슬링 시합을 걸고 있습니다.

translation.en: He is the greatest and strongest wrestler in all of Attica.
translation.kr: 그는 아티카 전체에서 가장 위대하고 강력한 레슬러입니다.

translation.en: He defeats every single challenger who steps forward.
translation.kr: 그는 앞으로 나서는 모든 도전자를 쓰러뜨립니다.

translation.en: Those he defeats are brutally and mercilessly murdered.
translation.kr: 그가 쓰러뜨린 자들은 잔인하고 무자비하게 살해당합니다.

translation.en: His palace courtyard is completely filled with their bones.
translation.kr: 그의 궁전 안뜰은 그들의 뼈로 가득 차 있습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus frowned, and said, ‘This seems indeed an ill-ruled land, and adventures enough in it to be tried.  But if I am the heir of it, I will rule it and right it, and here is my royal sceptre.’

translation.en: Theseus frowned deeply at their words.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그들의 말에 깊이 눈살을 찌푸렸습니다.

translation.en: This land seems poorly ruled indeed.
translation.kr: 이 땅은 참으로 엉망으로 다스려지고 있군요.

translation.en: There are plenty of adventures here to test my strength.
translation.kr: 내 힘을 시험할 모험이 이곳에 가득합니다.

translation.en: If I am the true heir to this land, I will fix it.
translation.kr: 내가 이 땅의 진정한 후계자라면 이 모든 것을 바로잡겠습니다.

translation.en: I will rule with justice, and this club is my royal scepter.
translation.kr: 나는 정의로 통치할 것이며, 이 몽둥이가 내 왕홀입니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And he shook his club of bronze, while the nymphs and shepherds clung round him, and entreated him not to go.

translation.en: He shook his heavy bronze club confidently.
translation.kr: 그는 무거운 청동 몽둥이를 자신 있게 흔들었습니다.

translation.en: The nymphs and shepherds clung to him.
translation.kr: 요정들과 양치기들은 그에게 매달렸습니다.

translation.en: They begged him desperately not to leave.
translation.kr: 그들은 제발 떠나지 말라고 간절히 애원했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But on he went nevertheless, till he could see both the seas and the citadel of Corinth towering high above all the land.  And he past swiftly along the Isthmus, for his heart burned to meet that cruel Sinis; and in a pine-wood at last he met him, where the Isthmus was narrowest and the road ran between high rocks.  There he sat upon a stone by the wayside, with a young fir-tree for a club across his knees, and a cord laid ready by his side; and over his head, upon the fir-tops, hung the bones of murdered men.

translation.en: But Theseus marched onward despite their warnings.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 그들의 경고에도 불구하고 앞으로 나아갔습니다.

translation.en: Soon he saw the two seas and the towering citadel of Corinth.
translation.kr: 이내 그는 두 바다와 높이 솟은 고린도의 성채를 보았습니다.

translation.en: He moved swiftly along the narrow Isthmus.
translation.kr: 그는 좁은 지협을 따라 빠르게 이동했습니다.

translation.en: His heart burned with eagerness to face the cruel Sinis.
translation.kr: 그의 마음은 잔인한 시니스와 맞서고 싶은 열망으로 불타올랐습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he spotted him in a dark pine wood.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 어두운 소나무 숲에서 그를 발견했습니다.

translation.en: It was where the Isthmus was narrowest between high rocks.
translation.kr: 그곳은 높은 바위들 사이로 지협이 가장 좁아지는 곳이었습니다.

translation.en: Sinis sat on a stone by the dusty wayside.
translation.kr: 시니스는 먼지 나는 길가 바위 위에 앉아 있었습니다.

translation.en: He rested a young pine tree across his knees like a club.
translation.kr: 그는 어린 소나무를 몽둥이처럼 무릎 위에 올려놓고 있었습니다.

translation.en: A thick rope lay ready on the ground beside him.
translation.kr: 그의 곁에는 두꺼운 밧줄이 바닥에 놓여 있었습니다.

translation.en: Human bones hung directly above his head in the tree branches.
translation.kr: 그의 머리 위 나뭇가지에는 사람의 뼈가 매달려 있었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus shouted to him, ‘Holla, thou valiant pine-bender, hast thou two fir-trees left for me?’

translation.en: Theseus shouted loudly to the giant.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 거인을 향해 큰 소리로 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Hello there, you brave Pine-Bender!
translation.kr: 이보시오, 용감한 소나무를 휘는 자여!

translation.en: Do you have two young pine trees left for me?
translation.kr: 나를 위해 어린 소나무 두 그루를 남겨두었소?

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And Sinis leapt to his feet, and answered, pointing to the bones above his head, ‘My larder has grown empty lately, so I have two fir-trees ready for thee.’  And he rushed on Theseus, lifting his club, and Theseus rushed upon him.

translation.en: Sinis leaped instantly to his feet.
translation.kr: 시니스는 즉시 자리에서 뛰어올랐습니다.

translation.en: He pointed grinning at the bones above his head.
translation.kr: 그는 씩 웃으며 머리 위의 뼈들을 가리켰습니다.

translation.en: My pantry has grown rather empty lately.
translation.kr: 내 식료품 창고가 요새 좀 비어 있었다네.

translation.en: So I have prepared two fine pine trees just for you!
translation.kr: 그래서 널 위해 좋은 소나무 두 그루를 준비해 두었지!

translation.en: He rushed violently at Theseus, swinging his tree.
translation.kr: 그는 나무를 휘두르며 테세우스를 향해 맹렬히 달려들었습니다.

translation.en: Theseus fearlessly charged right back at him.
translation.kr: 테세우스도 두려움 없이 그를 향해 곧장 돌진했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then they hammered together till the greenwoods rang; but the metal was tougher than the pine, and Sinis’ club broke right across, as the bronze came down upon it.  Then Theseus heaved up another mighty stroke, and smote Sinis down upon his face; and knelt upon his back, and bound him with his own cord, and said, ‘As thou hast done to others, so shall it be done to thee.’  Then he bent down two young fir-trees, and bound Sinis between them for all his struggling and his prayers; and let them go, and ended Sinis, and went on, leaving him to the hawks and crows.

translation.en: They clashed so hard that the green forest echoed.
translation.kr: 그들은 푸른 숲이 메아리칠 정도로 세게 부딪혔습니다.

translation.en: But the solid bronze was much tougher than the pine.
translation.kr: 하지만 단단한 청동은 소나무보다 훨씬 강했습니다.

translation.en: The bronze club smashed Sinis's tree completely in half.
translation.kr: 청동 몽둥이가 시니스의 나무를 완전히 반 동강 냈습니다.

translation.en: Theseus unleashed another massive, heavy strike.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 또 한 번의 거대하고 묵직한 일격을 가했습니다.

translation.en: He knocked Sinis flat onto his face.
translation.kr: 그는 시니스를 얼굴부터 바닥에 쓰러뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: Theseus knelt firmly on the giant's broad back.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 거인의 넓은 등 위에 단단히 무릎을 꿇었습니다.

translation.en: He bound Sinis tightly with the giant's own rope.
translation.kr: 그는 거인의 밧줄로 시니스를 단단히 묶었습니다.

translation.en: I will do to you exactly what you did to others.
translation.kr: 네가 다른 이들에게 했던 짓을 똑같이 갚아주겠다.

translation.en: He bent down two strong young pine trees.
translation.kr: 그는 튼튼하고 어린 소나무 두 그루를 구부렸습니다.

translation.en: He tied the struggling, begging Sinis between them.
translation.kr: 그는 발버둥 치며 애원하는 시니스를 나무 사이에 묶었습니다.

translation.en: Theseus let the trees snap back, instantly ending Sinis.
translation.kr: 테세우스가 나무를 놓자 시니스는 즉시 최후를 맞이했습니다.

translation.en: He walked away, leaving the body for the hawks and crows.
translation.kr: 그는 매와 까마귀를 위해 시체를 남겨두고 떠났습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then he went over the hills toward Megara, keeping close along the Saronic Sea, till he came to the cliffs of Sciron, and the narrow path between the mountain and the sea.

translation.en: Theseus traveled over the hills toward Megara.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 언덕을 넘어 메가라를 향해 이동했습니다.

translation.en: He stayed close to the edge of the Saronic Sea.
translation.kr: 그는 사로니코스 해변을 따라 바짝 붙어 걸었습니다.

translation.en: Soon he arrived at the dangerous cliffs of Sciron.
translation.kr: 이내 그는 스키론의 위험한 절벽에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: The path was dangerously narrow between the mountains and the sea.
translation.kr: 산과 바다 사이의 길은 아슬아슬할 정도로 좁았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And there he saw Sciron sitting by a fountain, at the edge of the cliff. On his knees was a mighty club; and he had barred the path with stones, so that every one must stop who came up.

translation.en: There he saw Sciron sitting lazily by a fountain.
translation.kr: 그곳에서 그는 스키론이 샘가에 게으르게 앉아 있는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: He rested at the very edge of the steep cliff.
translation.kr: 그는 가파른 절벽 끝자락에서 쉬고 있었습니다.

translation.en: A massive, heavy club rested on his knees.
translation.kr: 거대하고 무거운 몽둥이가 그의 무릎 위에 놓여 있었습니다.

translation.en: He had deliberately blocked the narrow path with rocks.
translation.kr: 그는 일부러 바위들로 좁은 길을 막아두었습니다.

translation.en: Every traveler who approached was forced to stop.
translation.kr: 다가오는 모든 여행자는 어쩔 수 없이 멈춰야만 했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus shouted to him, and said, ‘Holla, thou tortoise-feeder, do thy feet need washing to-day?’

translation.en: Theseus shouted loudly to the giant.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 거인을 향해 큰 소리로 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Hello there, you wicked tortoise-feeder!
translation.kr: 이보시오, 사악한 거북이 사육사!

translation.en: Do your dirty feet need washing today?
translation.kr: 오늘 네 더러운 발을 씻겨줄 사람이 필요하냐?

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And Sciron leapt to his feet, and answered—‘My tortoise is empty and hungry, and my feet need washing to-day.’  And he stood before his barrier, and lifted up his club in both hands.

translation.en: Sciron immediately leaped to his feet in anger.
translation.kr: 스키론은 분노하며 즉시 자리에서 뛰어올랐습니다.

translation.en: My tortoise is very empty and incredibly hungry!
translation.kr: 내 거북이는 속이 텅 비어서 엄청나게 굶주려 있다!

translation.en: And my feet definitely need washing today!
translation.kr: 그리고 내 발도 오늘 당장 씻어야겠어!

translation.en: He stood menacingly behind his rock barrier.
translation.kr: 그는 바위 장벽 뒤에 위협적으로 섰습니다.

translation.en: He lifted his massive club with both hands.
translation.kr: 그는 두 손으로 거대한 몽둥이를 들어 올렸습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus rushed upon him; and sore was the battle upon the cliff, for when Sciron felt the weight of the bronze club, he dropt his own, and closed with Theseus, and tried to hurl him by main force over the cliff. But Theseus was a wary wrestler, and dropt his own club, and caught him by the throat and by the knee, and forced him back against the wall of stones, and crushed him up against them, till his breath was almost gone. And Sciron cried panting, ‘Loose me, and I will let thee pass.’  But Theseus answered, ‘I must not pass till I have made the rough way smooth;’ and he forced him back against the wall till it fell, and Sciron rolled head over heels.

translation.en: Theseus rushed furiously at the giant.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 거인을 향해 맹렬히 돌진했습니다.

translation.en: A brutal battle began on the edge of the cliff.
translation.kr: 절벽 끝에서 잔혹한 전투가 시작되었습니다.

translation.en: Sciron quickly felt the crushing weight of the bronze club.
translation.kr: 스키론은 곧 청동 몽둥이의 끔찍한 무게를 느꼈습니다.

translation.en: Terrified, he dropped his own weapon and grappled with Theseus.
translation.kr: 겁에 질린 그는 자신의 무기를 버리고 테세우스와 맞붙었습니다.

translation.en: He tried to hurl Theseus entirely over the cliff by brute force.
translation.kr: 그는 엄청난 힘으로 테세우스를 절벽 아래로 던져버리려 했습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus was a clever and wary wrestler.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 영리하고 신중한 레슬러였습니다.

translation.en: He dropped his club and grabbed Sciron by the throat and knee.
translation.kr: 그는 몽둥이를 버리고 스키론의 목과 무릎을 움켜쥐었습니다.

translation.en: He violently forced the giant back against the rock barrier.
translation.kr: 그는 거인을 바위 장벽 쪽으로 난폭하게 밀어붙였습니다.

translation.en: He crushed him tightly until Sciron could barely breathe.
translation.kr: 스키론이 숨을 헐떡일 때까지 그를 강하게 짓눌렀습니다.

translation.en: Sciron gasped for air and begged for mercy.
translation.kr: 스키론은 숨을 헐떡이며 자비를 구했습니다.

translation.en: Let me go, and I will let you pass!
translation.kr: 나를 놓아다오, 그러면 네가 지나가게 해주마!

translation.en: But Theseus refused to let him go.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 그를 놓아주기를 거부했습니다.

translation.en: I cannot pass until I have made this rough road smooth!
translation.kr: 이 거친 길을 평탄하게 만들기 전에는 지나갈 수 없다!

translation.en: He forcefully pushed Sciron until the rock wall completely collapsed.
translation.kr: 그는 바위 벽이 완전히 무너질 때까지 스키론을 강하게 밀어붙였습니다.

translation.en: Sciron tumbled helplessly head over heels.
translation.kr: 스키론은 속수무책으로 거꾸로 고꾸라졌습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus lifted him up all bruised, and said, ‘Come hither and wash my feet.’  And he drew his sword, and sat down by the well, and said, ‘Wash my feet, or I cut you piecemeal.’

translation.en: Theseus yanked the bruised giant back to his feet.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 멍든 거인을 억지로 일으켜 세웠습니다.

translation.en: Come over here and wash my feet.
translation.kr: 이리 와서 내 발을 씻어라.

translation.en: Theseus drew his sharp sword and sat by the well.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 날카로운 칼을 뽑고 우물가에 앉았습니다.

translation.en: Wash my feet, or I will cut you into pieces.
translation.kr: 내 발을 씻어라, 그렇지 않으면 널 토막 내겠다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And Sciron washed his feet trembling; and when it was done, Theseus rose, and cried, ‘As thou hast done to others, so shall it be done to thee.  Go feed thy tortoise thyself;’ and he kicked him over the cliff into the sea.

translation.en: Sciron trembled in fear as he washed Theseus's feet.
translation.kr: 스키론은 공포에 떨며 테세우스의 발을 씻겼습니다.

translation.en: When the task was fully finished, Theseus stood up.
translation.kr: 그 일이 완전히 끝나자 테세우스가 일어섰습니다.

translation.en: I will do to you exactly what you did to others.
translation.kr: 네가 다른 이들에게 했던 짓을 똑같이 갚아주겠다.

translation.en: Go down and feed your hungry tortoise yourself!
translation.kr: 내려가서 네 굶주린 거북이에게 직접 먹이가 되어라!

translation.en: Theseus violently kicked him over the cliff into the sea.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그를 세게 걷어차 절벽 아래 바다로 떨어뜨렸습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And whether the tortoise ate him, I know not; for some say that earth and sea both disdained to take his body, so foul it was with sin.  So the sea cast it out upon the shore, and the shore cast it back into the sea, and at last the waves hurled it high into the air in anger; and it hung there long without a grave, till it was changed into a desolate rock, which stands there in the surge until this day.

translation.en: I do not know if the giant tortoise actually ate him.
translation.kr: 거대한 거북이가 정말로 그를 먹었는지는 알 수 없습니다.

translation.en: Some say the earth and sea both refused to take his body.
translation.kr: 어떤 이들은 땅과 바다 모두 그의 시신을 거부했다고 말합니다.

translation.en: He was far too foul and polluted with terrible sins.
translation.kr: 그는 끔찍한 죄악으로 너무나도 더럽고 타락했기 때문입니다.

translation.en: The sea spat his body out onto the sandy shore.
translation.kr: 바다는 그의 시신을 모래사장으로 뱉어냈습니다.

translation.en: The shore immediately tossed it back into the restless sea.
translation.kr: 해안은 즉시 그것을 다시 요동치는 바다로 던져버렸습니다.

translation.en: Finally, the angry waves hurled it high into the open air.
translation.kr: 마침내 성난 파도가 그것을 허공 높이 내동댕이쳤습니다.

translation.en: It hung there for a long time without a proper grave.
translation.kr: 그것은 제대로 된 무덤도 없이 오랫동안 그곳에 매달려 있었습니다.

translation.en: Eventually, it was transformed into a desolate, jagged rock.
translation.kr: 결국 그것은 황량하고 뾰족한 바위로 변했습니다.

translation.en: That rock still stands in the crashing surf today.
translation.kr: 그 바위는 오늘날까지도 부서지는 파도 속에 서 있습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: This at least is true, which Pausanias tells, that in the royal porch at Athens he saw the figure of Theseus modelled in clay, and by him Sciron the robber falling headlong into the sea.

translation.en: At least one thing told by Pausanias is entirely true.
translation.kr: 파우사니아스가 전한 이야기 중 적어도 한 가지는 완전히 사실입니다.

translation.en: He saw a clay statue of Theseus in the royal porch at Athens.
translation.kr: 그는 아테네의 왕실 현관에서 테세우스의 점토 조각상을 보았습니다.

translation.en: Beside it fell the robber Sciron, plunging headlong into the sea.
translation.kr: 그 옆에는 바다로 곤두박질치는 도적 스키론의 모습이 있었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then he went a long day’s journey, past Megara, into the Attic land, and high before him rose the snow-peaks of Cithæron, all cold above the black pine-woods, where haunt the Furies, and the raving Bacchæ, and the Nymphs who drive men wild, far aloft upon the dreary mountains, where the storms howl all day long.  And on his right hand was the sea always, and Salamis, with its island cliffs, and the sacred strait of the sea-fight, where afterwards the Persians fled before the Greeks.  So he went all day until the evening, till he saw the Thriasian plain, and the sacred city of Eleusis, where the Earth-mother’s temple stands.  For there she met Triptolemus, when all the land lay waste, Demeter the kind Earth-mother, and in her hands a sheaf of corn.  And she taught him to plough the fallows, and to yoke the lazy kine; and she taught him to sow the seed-fields, and to reap the golden grain; and sent him forth to teach all nations, and give corn to labouring men.  So at Eleusis all men honour her, whosoever tills the land; her and Triptolemus her beloved, who gave corn to labouring men.

translation.en: Theseus walked for a long day past Megara into Attica.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 하루 종일 걸어 메가라를 지나 아티카로 들어갔습니다.

translation.en: The freezing snow peaks of Cithaeron rose high before him.
translation.kr: 키타이론의 얼어붙은 설봉이 그의 눈앞에 높이 솟아 있었습니다.

translation.en: They loomed cold above the dark, black pine woods.
translation.kr: 그것들은 짙고 검은 소나무 숲 위로 차갑게 우뚝 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: The Furies and the raving Bacchantes haunted those wild places.
translation.kr: 복수의 여신들과 광란의 바쿠스 신도들이 그 거친 곳에 출몰했습니다.

translation.en: Nymphs who drove men mad lived high in the dreary mountains.
translation.kr: 사람들을 미치게 하는 요정들이 황량한 산꼭대기에 살았습니다.

translation.en: Fierce storms howled there violently all day long.
translation.kr: 그곳에서는 사나운 폭풍이 하루 종일 맹렬하게 울부짖었습니다.

translation.en: The sea was always crashing on his right side.
translation.kr: 그의 오른쪽에는 항상 바다가 철썩이고 있었습니다.

translation.en: He passed Salamis with its majestic island cliffs.
translation.kr: 그는 장엄한 섬 절벽이 있는 살라미스를 지났습니다.

translation.en: He saw the sacred strait where the great sea battle happened.
translation.kr: 그는 훗날 위대한 해전이 벌어진 신성한 해협을 보았습니다.

translation.en: That is where the Persians later fled from the Greeks.
translation.kr: 그곳은 나중에 페르시아군이 그리스군을 피해 달아난 곳입니다.

translation.en: He walked all day until the calm evening arrived.
translation.kr: 그는 고요한 저녁이 올 때까지 하루 종일 걸었습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he saw the fertile Thriasian plain.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 비옥한 트리아시아 평원을 보았습니다.

translation.en: He reached Eleusis, where the Earth-Mother's temple stands.
translation.kr: 그는 대지의 어머니 신전이 있는 엘레우시스에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: Demeter had met Triptolemus there when the land was barren.
translation.kr: 데메테르는 땅이 황폐했을 때 그곳에서 트립톨레모스를 만났습니다.

translation.en: The kind Earth-Mother held a golden sheaf of corn.
translation.kr: 다정한 대지의 어머니는 황금빛 옥수수 단을 들고 있었습니다.

translation.en: She taught him how to plow the unplanted fields.
translation.kr: 그녀는 씨를 뿌리지 않은 들판을 쟁기질하는 법을 가르쳤습니다.

translation.en: She showed him how to yoke the lazy, stubborn cattle.
translation.kr: 그녀는 게으르고 고집 센 소들에게 멍에를 씌우는 법을 보여주었습니다.

translation.en: She taught him to sow seeds and reap the golden grain.
translation.kr: 그녀는 씨를 뿌리고 황금빛 곡식을 수확하는 법을 가르쳤습니다.

translation.en: She sent him to teach all nations and feed working men.
translation.kr: 그녀는 모든 민족을 가르치고 일하는 자들을 먹이도록 그를 보냈습니다.

translation.en: So at Eleusis, all farmers deeply honor her.
translation.kr: 그래서 엘레우시스에서는 땅을 일구는 모든 이가 그녀를 깊이 공경합니다.

translation.en: They honor her and her beloved Triptolemus, who gave them corn.
translation.kr: 그들은 그녀와 사람들에게 옥수수를 준 사랑하는 트립톨레모스를 공경합니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And he went along the plain into Eleusis, and stood in the market-place, and cried—

translation.en: Theseus walked proudly across the plain into Eleusis.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 당당하게 평원을 가로질러 엘레우시스로 들어갔습니다.

translation.en: He stood boldly in the busy marketplace and shouted.
translation.kr: 그는 붐비는 시장 한가운데 대담하게 서서 외쳤습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Where is Kerkuon, the king of the city?  I must wrestle a fall with him to-day.’

translation.en: Where is Cercyon, the cruel king of this city?
translation.kr: 이 도시의 잔인한 왕 케르키온은 어디에 있느냐?

translation.en: I must wrestle a terrible match with him today!
translation.kr: 나는 오늘 그와 목숨을 건 레슬링 시합을 해야겠다!

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then all the people crowded round him, and cried, ‘Fair youth, why will you die?  Hasten out of the city, before the cruel king hears that a stranger is here.’

translation.en: The terrified people quickly crowded around him.
translation.kr: 겁에 질린 사람들이 재빨리 그의 주위로 몰려들었습니다.

translation.en: Fair youth, why do you wish to die so soon?
translation.kr: 아름다운 청년이여, 어찌하여 이리 일찍 죽으려 하십니까?

translation.en: Hurry out of the city before the cruel king hears!
translation.kr: 잔인한 왕이 이방인의 소식을 듣기 전에 어서 도시를 빠져나가십시오!

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But Theseus went up through the town, while the people wept and prayed, and through the gates of the palace-yard, and through the piles of bones and skulls, till he came to the door of Kerkuon’s hall, the terror of all mortal men.

translation.en: But Theseus boldly walked further up into the town.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 대담하게 마을 위쪽으로 걸어 올라갔습니다.

translation.en: The frightened people wept and prayed for his life.
translation.kr: 겁에 질린 사람들은 그의 목숨을 위해 눈물을 흘리며 기도했습니다.

translation.en: He passed through the massive gates of the palace yard.
translation.kr: 그는 궁전 안뜰의 거대한 문을 통과했습니다.

translation.en: He walked through disgusting piles of bones and skulls.
translation.kr: 그는 끔찍한 뼈와 해골 더미 사이를 걸어갔습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he reached the heavy door of Cercyon's hall.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 케르키온 전당의 무거운 문에 다다랐습니다.

translation.en: That place was the absolute terror of all mortal men.
translation.kr: 그곳은 모든 인간들에게 절대적인 공포의 장소였습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And there he saw Kerkuon sitting at the table in the hall alone; and before him was a whole sheep roasted, and beside him a whole jar of wine. And Theseus stood and called him, ‘Holla, thou valiant wrestler, wilt thou wrestle a fall to-day?’

translation.en: There he saw Cercyon sitting entirely alone at a table.
translation.kr: 그곳에서 그는 케르키온이 식탁에 완전히 홀로 앉아 있는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: Before him lay a massive whole roasted sheep.
translation.kr: 그의 앞에는 거대한 양 통구이가 놓여 있었습니다.

translation.en: Beside him sat a huge, heavy jar of wine.
translation.kr: 그의 곁에는 크고 무거운 포도주 항아리가 있었습니다.

translation.en: Theseus stood tall and called out to him.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 당당하게 서서 그를 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Hello there, you valiantly brutal wrestler!
translation.kr: 이보시오, 잔인하리만치 용맹한 레슬러여!

translation.en: Will you wrestle a deadly match with me today?
translation.kr: 오늘 나와 목숨을 건 시합을 하겠소?

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And Kerkuon looked up and laughed, and answered, ‘I will wrestle a fall to-day; but come in, for I am lonely and thou weary, and eat and drink before thou die.’

translation.en: Cercyon looked up slowly and let out a wicked laugh.
translation.kr: 케르키온은 천천히 고개를 들고 사악한 웃음을 터뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: I will certainly wrestle a fall with you today.
translation.kr: 오늘 너와 기꺼이 시합을 해주마.

translation.en: But come inside, for I am lonely and you are tired.
translation.kr: 하지만 안으로 들어오너라, 나는 외롭고 너는 지쳐 보이니.

translation.en: Eat and drink well before you inevitably die.
translation.kr: 피할 수 없는 죽음을 맞이하기 전에 실컷 먹고 마셔라.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus went up boldly, and sat down before Kerkuon at the board; and he ate his fill of the sheep’s flesh, and drank his fill of the wine; and Theseus ate enough for three men, but Kerkuon ate enough for seven.

translation.en: Theseus stepped up boldly and sat across from Kerkuon at the table.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 담대하게 나아가 탁자에 앉아 케르키온과 마주 보았습니다.

translation.en: He ate his fill of mutton and drank plenty of wine.
translation.kr: 그는 양고기를 실컷 먹고 포도주도 양껏 마셨습니다.

translation.en: Theseus ate enough for three men, but Kerkuon ate enough for seven.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 장정 세 명의 몫을 먹어치웠으나, 케르키온은 일곱 명의 몫을 먹었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But neither spoke a word to the other, though they looked across the table by stealth; and each said in his heart, ‘He has broad shoulders; but I trust mine are as broad as his.’

translation.en: Neither spoke a word, though they stole glances at each other across the table.
translation.kr: 두 사람은 탁자 너머로 서로를 훔쳐보면서도 아무 말도 하지 않았습니다.

translation.en: Each man thought to himself, He has broad shoulders, but mine are just as broad.
translation.kr: 각자 마음속으로 저 자의 어깨가 떡 벌어지긴 했지만 내 어깨도 저만큼은 넓지라고 생각했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: At last, when the sheep was eaten and the jar of wine drained dry, King Kerkuon rose, and cried, ‘Let us wrestle a fall before we sleep.’

translation.en: Finally, when the meat was gone and the wine jar empty, King Kerkuon stood up.
translation.kr: 마침내 양고기가 다 떨어지고 포도주 항아리마저 바닥을 드러내자 케르키온 왕이 자리에서 일어났습니다.

translation.en: Let us wrestle a match before we sleep, he shouted.
translation.kr: 잠들기 전에 레슬링으로 승부를 가려보자꾸나 하고 그가 소리쳤습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: So they tossed off all their garments, and went forth in the palace-yard; and Kerkuon bade strew fresh sand in an open space between the bones.

translation.en: They tossed off their clothes and went out into the courtyard.
translation.kr: 두 사람은 옷을 훌렁 벗어 던지고 궁전 안뜰로 나갔습니다.

translation.en: Kerkuon ordered fresh sand to be scattered in an open space among the scattered bones.
translation.kr: 케르키온은 뼈들이 흩어진 공터에 깨끗한 모래를 깔라고 명령했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And there the heroes stood face to face, while their eyes glared like wild bulls’; and all the people crowded at the gates to see what would befall.

translation.en: The two men stood face to face, their eyes glaring like wild bulls.
translation.kr: 두 사내는 야생 황소처럼 눈을 부라리며 서로 마주 섰습니다.

translation.en: All the people crowded around the gates to see what would happen.
translation.kr: 모든 사람들이 무슨 일이 벌어질지 보려고 성문 주변으로 몰려들었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And there they stood and wrestled, till the stars shone out above their heads; up and down and round, till the sand was stamped hard beneath their feet.  And their eyes flashed like stars in the darkness, and their breath went up like smoke in the night air; but neither took nor gave a footstep, and the people watched silent at the gates.

translation.en: They stood and wrestled until the stars appeared above them.
translation.kr: 그들은 머리 위로 별이 뜰 때까지 서서 레슬링을 했습니다.

translation.en: They struggled up and down, stamping the sand hard beneath their feet.
translation.kr: 두 사람은 이리저리 뒤엉키며 모래바닥이 단단하게 다져지도록 짓밟았습니다.

translation.en: Their eyes flashed in the darkness, and their breath rose like smoke in the night air.
translation.kr: 어둠 속에서 그들의 두 눈은 번뜩였고 내뿜는 숨결은 밤공기에 연기처럼 피어올랐습니다.

translation.en: Neither man gave an inch, and the crowd watched in silence.
translation.kr: 두 사람 모두 한 치의 양보도 없었고 군중은 숨을 죽인 채 지켜보았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But at last Kerkuon grew angry, and caught Theseus round the neck, and shook him as a mastiff shakes a rat; but he could not shake him off his feet.

translation.en: At last Kerkuon grew angry and caught Theseus around the neck.
translation.kr: 마침내 화가 치밀어 오른 케르키온이 테세우스의 목을 부여잡았습니다.

translation.en: He shook him like a dog shakes a rat, but he could not knock him off his feet.
translation.kr: 그는 개가 쥐를 흔들듯 그를 마구 흔들어 댔지만 테세우스를 쓰러뜨리지는 못했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But Theseus was quick and wary, and clasped Kerkuon round the waist, and slipped his loin quickly underneath him, while he caught him by the wrist; and then he hove a mighty heave, a heave which would have stirred an oak, and lifted Kerkuon, and pitched him right over his shoulder on the ground.

translation.en: Theseus was quick and cautious.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 재빠르고 신중했습니다.

translation.en: He grabbed Kerkuon around the waist and quickly slipped beneath him.
translation.kr: 그는 케르키온의 허리를 끌어안고는 잽싸게 그의 몸통 밑으로 파고들었습니다.

translation.en: Catching the king by the wrist, he delivered a mighty heave that could uproot an oak.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 왕의 손목을 낚아채고 떡갈나무라도 뽑아버릴 듯한 괴력으로 밀어올렸습니다.

translation.en: He lifted Kerkuon and pitched him right over his shoulder onto the ground.
translation.kr: 그는 케르키온을 번쩍 들어 자신의 어깨 너머로 바닥에 내동댕이쳤습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then he leapt on him, and called, ‘Yield, or I kill thee!’ but Kerkuon said no word; for his heart was burst within him with the fall, and the meat, and the wine.

translation.en: Theseus leaped onto him and yelled, Yield, or I will kill you!
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그 위로 올라타서 항복하라, 그렇지 않으면 목숨을 끊겠다고 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: But Kerkuon said nothing, for his heart had burst from the heavy fall, the meat, and the wine.
translation.kr: 하지만 케르키온은 아무 대답이 없었는데, 엄청난 충격과 잔뜩 먹어댄 고기와 포도주 때문에 심장이 터져버렸기 때문입니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus opened the gates, and called in all the people; and they cried, ‘You have slain our evil king; be you now our king, and rule us well.’

translation.en: Theseus opened the gates and called all the people inside.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 성문을 열고 백성들을 모두 안으로 불러 모았습니다.

translation.en: You have killed our evil king, they cried.
translation.kr: 당신이 우리의 사악한 왕을 물리쳤소 하고 그들이 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Please be our king now and rule us well.
translation.kr: 이제 우리의 왕이 되어 우리를 잘 다스려 주십시오.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘I will be your king in Eleusis, and I will rule you right and well; for this cause I have slain all evil-doers—Sinis, and Sciron, and this man last of all.’

translation.en: I will be your king in Eleusis, and I will rule you justly.
translation.kr: 내가 엘레우시스에서 여러분의 왕이 되어 공정하게 다스리겠습니다.

translation.en: This is why I have slain all these evildoers, Sinis, Sciron, and finally this man.
translation.kr: 시니스와 스키론, 그리고 마침내 이 자까지 사악한 무리들을 모두 처단한 것도 바로 그 때문입니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then an aged man stepped forth, and said, ‘Young hero, hast thou slain Sinis?  Beware then of Ægeus, king of Athens, to whom thou goest, for he is near of kin to Sinis.’

translation.en: Then an old man stepped forward.
translation.kr: 그때 한 노인이 앞으로 나섰습니다.

translation.en: Young hero, have you killed Sinis? he asked.
translation.kr: 젊은 영웅이여, 시니스를 물리쳤단 말이오? 하고 그가 물었습니다.

translation.en: Beware of Aegeus, the king of Athens, to whom you travel.
translation.kr: 당신이 찾아가려는 아테네의 왕 아이게우스를 조심하시오.

translation.en: He is a close relative of Sinis.
translation.kr: 그는 시니스와 가까운 친척이라오.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Then I have slain my own kinsman,’ said Theseus, ‘though well he deserved to die.  Who will purge me from his death, for rightfully I slew him, unrighteous and accursed as he was?’

translation.en: Then I have killed my own relative, Theseus said, though he certainly deserved to die.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 내 핏줄을 내 손으로 죽였단 말이군 하고 테세우스가 말하길, 비록 그가 죽어 마땅한 자이긴 했지만 말이오 했습니다.

translation.en: Who will purify me of his blood?
translation.kr: 누가 이 피의 죄악을 씻어 주겠소?

translation.en: I killed him rightfully, for he was wicked and cursed.
translation.kr: 그는 사악하고 저주받은 자였기에 나는 정당하게 그를 물리쳤단 말이오.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And the old man answered—

translation.en: The old man replied.
translation.kr: 노인이 대답했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘That will the heroes do, the sons of Phytalus, who dwell beneath the elm-tree in Aphidnai, by the bank of silver Cephisus; for they know the mysteries of the Gods.  Thither you shall go and be purified, and after you shall be our king.’

translation.en: The heroes will do that.
translation.kr: 그 일은 영웅들이 해 줄 것이오.

translation.en: They are the sons of Phytalus, who live beneath the elm tree in Aphidnai by the silver Cephisus river.
translation.kr: 그들은 은빛 케피수스 강변 아피드나이의 느릅나무 아래에 사는 피탈로스의 아들들이라오.

translation.en: They know the mysteries of the gods.
translation.kr: 그들은 신들의 신비로운 의식을 잘 알고 있지요.

translation.en: You must go there to be purified, and afterward you shall be our king.
translation.kr: 그곳으로 가서 정화 의식을 치른 뒤에 돌아와 우리의 왕이 되어 주시오.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: So he took an oath of the people of Eleusis, that they would serve him as their king, and went away next morning across the Thriasian plain, and over the hills toward Aphidnai, that he might find the sons of Phytalus.

translation.en: Theseus made the people of Eleusis swear an oath to serve him as king.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 엘레우시스 백성들에게 자신을 왕으로 섬기겠다는 맹세를 받았습니다.

translation.en: The next morning, he set out across the Thriasian plain and over the hills toward Aphidnai to find the sons of Phytalus.
translation.kr: 다음 날 아침, 그는 피탈로스의 아들들을 찾기 위해 트리아시아 평원을 가로질러 언덕을 넘어 아피드나이를 향해 길을 나섰습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And as he was skirting the Vale of Cephisus, along the foot of lofty Parnes, a very tall and strong man came down to meet him, dressed in rich garments.  On his arms were golden bracelets, and round his neck a collar of jewels; and he came forward, bowing courteously, and held out both his hands, and spoke—

translation.en: As he skirted the edge of the valley along the foot of Mount Parnes, a tall, strong man approached him.
translation.kr: 그가 우뚝 솟은 파르네스 산기슭을 따라 계곡 가장자리를 돌고 있을 때, 키가 크고 건장한 남자가 다가왔습니다.

translation.en: He was dressed in rich clothes, wearing golden bracelets and a jeweled collar.
translation.kr: 그는 값비싼 옷을 입고 양팔에는 금팔찌를 두르고 목에는 보석 목걸이를 걸고 있었습니다.

translation.en: The man came forward, bowing politely, held out his hands, and spoke.
translation.kr: 남자는 앞으로 다가와 정중하게 고개 숙여 인사하고는 두 손을 내밀며 말했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Welcome, fair youth, to these mountains; happy am I to have met you! For what greater pleasure to a good man, than to entertain strangers? But I see that you are weary.  Come up to my castle, and rest yourself awhile.’

translation.en: Welcome to these mountains, young man. I am happy to meet you!
translation.kr: 이 깊은 산속에 오신 것을 환영하오 젊은이. 만나게 되어 참으로 기쁘구려!

translation.en: What greater pleasure is there for a good man than to entertain strangers?
translation.kr: 선한 사람에게 낯선 나그네를 대접하는 것보다 더 큰 기쁨이 어디 있겠소?

translation.en: I can see that you are tired.
translation.kr: 보아하니 몹시 지친 것 같소만.

translation.en: Come up to my castle and rest for a while.
translation.kr: 내 성으로 올라가서 잠시 쉬어 가시지요.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘I give you thanks,’ said Theseus: ‘but I am in haste to go up the valley, and to reach Aphidnai in the Vale of Cephisus.’

translation.en: Thank you, Theseus replied, but I am in a hurry.
translation.kr: 감사합니다 하고 테세우스가 답하길, 하지만 저는 갈 길이 바쁩니다 했습니다.

translation.en: I need to travel up the valley and reach Aphidnai.
translation.kr: 계곡을 따라 올라가 아피드나이에 서둘러 당도해야 하거든요.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Alas! you have wandered far from the right way, and you cannot reach Aphidnai to-night, for there are many miles of mountain between you and it, and steep passes, and cliffs dangerous after nightfall.  It is well for you that I met you, for my whole joy is to find strangers, and to feast them at my castle, and hear tales from them of foreign lands.  Come up with me, and eat the best of venison, and drink the rich red wine, and sleep upon my famous bed, of which all travellers say that they never saw the like.  For whatsoever the stature of my guest, however tall or short, that bed fits him to a hair, and he sleeps on it as he never slept before.’  And he laid hold on Theseus’ hands, and would not let him go.

translation.en: Alas! You have wandered far from the right path.
translation.kr: 이런! 길을 단단히 잘못 드셨구려.

translation.en: You cannot reach Aphidnai tonight, for miles of steep passes and dangerous cliffs lie ahead.
translation.kr: 가파른 고갯길과 위험한 절벽이 까마득히 이어져 있어 오늘 밤엔 아피드나이에 절대 닿지 못할 거요.

translation.en: It is a good thing I found you, for my greatest joy is feasting strangers in my castle and hearing their tales.
translation.kr: 나를 만난 게 참으로 다행이지 않소. 낯선 사람들을 성으로 데려가 잔치를 베풀고 그들의 모험담을 듣는 것이 내 유일한 낙이라오.

translation.en: Come with me to eat the best venison and drink rich red wine.
translation.kr: 나와 함께 가서 최고급 사슴고기를 맛보고 향긋한 붉은 포도주도 마시도록 합시다.

translation.en: You can sleep upon my famous bed, which travelers say is unlike any other.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 여행자들 사이에서 칭송이 자자한 내 특별한 침대에 누워 푹 쉬시구려.

translation.en: Whether a guest is tall or short, the bed fits him perfectly, giving him the best sleep of his life.
translation.kr: 키가 크든 작든 손님의 체격에 머리카락 하나 안 틀리고 딱 맞춘 듯해서 평생 처음 겪는 달콤한 잠을 선사한다오.

translation.en: The man grabbed Theseus by the hands and would not let him go.
translation.kr: 남자는 테세우스의 손을 부여잡고는 결코 놓아주려 하지 않았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Theseus wished to go forwards: but he was ashamed to seem churlish to so hospitable a man; and he was curious to see that wondrous bed; and beside, he was hungry and weary: yet he shrank from the man, he knew not why; for, though his voice was gentle and fawning, it was dry and husky like a toad’s; and though his eyes were gentle, they were dull and cold like stones.  But he consented, and went with the man up a glen which led from the road toward the peaks of Parnes, under the dark shadow of the cliffs.

translation.en: Theseus wanted to keep moving, but he felt bad refusing such a welcoming host.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 계속 길을 재촉하고 싶었지만 이렇게 환대해 주는 사람에게 무례하게 굴기가 미안했습니다.

translation.en: He was also hungry, tired, and curious to see this wondrous bed.
translation.kr: 게다가 배도 고프고 몹시 지쳐 있던 터라 그 신기한 침대를 한번 보고 싶은 호기심도 생겼습니다.

translation.en: Still, something about the man made him hesitate.
translation.kr: 그럼에도 웬일인지 그 남자에게서 묘한 거부감이 느껴졌습니다.

translation.en: His voice was gentle but dry and husky like a toad, and his eyes were dull and cold as stone.
translation.kr: 그의 목소리는 부드럽고 상냥했지만 두꺼비처럼 건조하고 쇳소리가 났으며, 눈빛 또한 친절해 보이면서도 돌멩이처럼 탁하고 차가웠기 때문입니다.

translation.en: Finally, Theseus agreed and followed the man up a narrow valley toward the dark cliffs of Mount Parnes.
translation.kr: 결국 테세우스는 그를 따라 굽이진 길을 지나 파르네스의 산봉우리를 향해 드리워진 짙은 절벽 그림자 아래 좁은 골짜기로 들어섰습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And as they went up, the glen grew narrower, and the cliffs higher and darker, and beneath them a torrent roared, half seen between bare limestone crags.  And around there was neither tree nor bush, while from the white peaks of Parnes the snow-blasts swept down the glen, cutting and chilling till a horror fell on Theseus as he looked round at that doleful place.  And he asked at last, ‘Your castle stands, it seems, in a dreary region.’

translation.en: As they climbed, the valley grew narrower, and the cliffs loomed higher and darker.
translation.kr: 위로 올라갈수록 골짜기는 더욱 좁아지고 절벽은 한층 더 높고 어두컴컴해졌습니다.

translation.en: A roaring torrent flowed far below them through the bare limestone rocks.
translation.kr: 저 아래 앙상한 석회암 바위들 틈새로는 세찬 급류가 소리치며 흐르고 있었습니다.

translation.en: There were no trees or bushes, and freezing wind swept down from the snowy peaks.
translation.kr: 주변엔 나무 한 그루, 덤불 하나 찾아볼 수 없었고 하얗게 눈 덮인 산봉우리에서 불어온 매서운 눈보라가 골짜기를 할퀴듯 몰아쳤습니다.

translation.en: A sense of dread fell upon Theseus as he looked around the gloomy place.
translation.kr: 그 을씨년스러운 풍경을 둘러보던 테세우스의 마음에 왠지 모를 두려움이 엄습했습니다.

translation.en: He finally said, It seems your castle stands in a rather dreary region.
translation.kr: 결국 그가 입을 열어 댁의 성은 다소 음산한 곳에 자리 잡고 있군요 하고 말했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Yes; but once within it, hospitality makes all things cheerful.  But who are these?’ and he looked back, and Theseus also; and far below, along the road which they had left, came a string of laden asses, and merchants walking by them, watching their ware.

translation.en: Yes, but once inside, my hospitality makes everything cheerful.
translation.kr: 그렇긴 하지만 일단 성에 들어서서 대접을 받다 보면 모든 게 즐거워질 거요.

translation.en: But who are these people? the man asked, looking back.
translation.kr: 아니, 저 사람들은 누굴까? 하고 남자가 뒤를 돌아보며 물었습니다.

translation.en: Theseus looked down and saw merchants leading loaded donkeys along the road below.
translation.kr: 테세우스도 뒤를 돌아 저 멀리 아래쪽 길을 내려다보니 상인들이 물건을 잔뜩 짊어진 당나귀들을 줄지어 몰고 오고 있었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Ah, poor souls!’ said the stranger.  ‘Well for them that I looked back and saw them!  And well for me too, for I shall have the more guests at my feast.  Wait awhile till I go down and call them, and we will eat and drink together the livelong night.  Happy am I, to whom Heaven sends so many guests at once!’

translation.en: Ah, the poor souls! said the stranger.
translation.kr: 아, 가엾은 사람들! 하고 남자가 말했습니다.

translation.en: It is a good thing I looked back and saw them!
translation.kr: 내가 뒤를 돌아봐서 저들을 발견했으니 참으로 다행이오!

translation.en: It is good for me too, for I will have more guests at my feast.
translation.kr: 내 잔치에 손님이 더 늘게 되었으니 나에게도 좋은 일이지요.

translation.en: Wait here while I go down and call them, so we can all eat and drink together tonight.
translation.kr: 내가 내려가 저들을 데려올 테니 여기서 잠시만 기다리시오, 그러면 밤새도록 다 함께 먹고 마실 수 있을 거요.

translation.en: I am so lucky that heaven has sent me all these guests at once!
translation.kr: 하늘이 이렇게 한꺼번에 많은 손님을 보내 주시다니 나는 정말 운이 좋은 사람이오!

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And he ran back down the hill, waving his hand and shouting, to the merchants, while Theseus went slowly up the steep pass.

translation.en: He ran back down the hill, waving his hand and shouting to the merchants.
translation.kr: 그는 언덕 아래로 달려 내려가 상인들을 향해 손을 흔들며 크게 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Meanwhile, Theseus continued slowly up the steep mountain pass.
translation.kr: 그사이 테세우스는 가파른 산길을 따라 천천히 걸어 올라갔습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But as he went up he met an aged man, who had been gathering drift-wood in the torrent-bed.  He had laid down his faggot in the road, and was trying to lift it again to his shoulder.  And when he saw Theseus, he called to him, and said—

translation.en: As he climbed, he met an old man who had been gathering firewood from the riverbed.
translation.kr: 계속 걸어 올라가던 그는 강바닥에서 땔감을 줍고 있던 한 노인과 마주쳤습니다.

translation.en: The man had set his bundle down and was struggling to lift it back onto his shoulder.
translation.kr: 노인은 장작단을 길바닥에 내려놓고 다시 어깨에 짊어지려고 몹시 쩔쩔매고 있었습니다.

translation.en: When he saw Theseus, he called out to him.
translation.kr: 테세우스를 본 그가 소리쳐 불렀습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘O fair youth, help me up with my burden, for my limbs are stiff and weak with years.’

translation.en: Young man, please help me lift my burden.
translation.kr: 젊은이, 이 짐을 올리는 것 좀 도와주구려.

translation.en: My limbs are stiff and weak with age.
translation.kr: 나이가 들어 팔다리가 뻣뻣하고 기운이 하나도 없어서 그렇소.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus lifted the burden on his back.  And the old man blest him, and then looked earnestly upon him, and said—

translation.en: Theseus lifted the burden onto his back.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 짐을 등 위로 들어 올렸습니다.

translation.en: The old man blessed him, looked earnestly at him, and spoke.
translation.kr: 노인은 그를 축복하고 진지하게 바라보며 말했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Who are you, fair youth, and wherefore travel you this doleful road?’

translation.en: Who are you, fair youth, and why do you travel this sorrowful road?
translation.kr: 아름다운 젊은이여, 당신은 누구이며 왜 이 슬픈 길을 여행하고 있습니까?

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Who I am my parents know; but I travel this doleful road because I have been invited by a hospitable man, who promises to feast me, and to make me sleep upon I know not what wondrous bed.’

translation.en: My parents know who I am.
translation.kr: 제 부모님은 제가 누구인지 알고 계십니다.

translation.en: But I travel this sad road because a hospitable man invited me.
translation.kr: 하지만 어떤 친절한 남자가 저를 초대했기 때문에 이 슬픈 길을 여행하고 있습니다.

translation.en: He promised to feast me and let me sleep on some wondrous bed.
translation.kr: 그는 저를 대접하고 어떤 놀라운 침대에서 재워주겠다고 약속했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then the old man clapped his hands together and cried—

translation.en: The old man clapped his hands together and cried out.
translation.kr: 그러자 노인은 두 손을 마주치며 소리쳤습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘O house of Hades, man-devouring! will thy maw never be full?  Know, fair youth, that you are going to torment and to death, for he who met you (I will requite your kindness by another) is a robber and a murderer of men. Whatsoever stranger he meets he entices him hither to death; and as for this bed of which he speaks, truly it fits all comers, yet none ever rose alive off it save me.’

translation.en: Oh, man-devouring house of Hades!
translation.kr: 아, 사람을 집어삼키는 하데스의 집이여!

translation.en: Will your stomach never be full?
translation.kr: 당신의 배는 영원히 채워지지 않을 것입니까?

translation.en: Know this, fair youth, you are heading to torment and death.
translation.kr: 아름다운 젊은이여, 당신은 고통과 죽음을 향해 가고 있다는 것을 아십시오.

translation.en: I will return your kindness by warning you.
translation.kr: 당신의 친절에 보답하기 위해 경고하겠습니다.

translation.en: The man who met you is a robber and a murderer.
translation.kr: 당신이 만난 남자는 강도이자 살인마입니다.

translation.en: He entices every stranger he meets here to their death.
translation.kr: 그는 만나는 모든 낯선 사람들을 이곳으로 유인하여 죽입니다.

translation.en: As for that bed he speaks of, it truly fits all comers.
translation.kr: 그가 말하는 그 침대는 모든 방문객에게 딱 맞습니다.

translation.en: Yet no one has ever risen alive from it except me.
translation.kr: 하지만 나를 제외하고는 아무도 그곳에서 살아서 일어난 적이 없습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Why?’ asked Theseus, astonished.

translation.en: Why? asked Theseus, astonished.
translation.kr: 왜입니까? 테세우스가 깜짝 놀라 물었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Because, if a man be too tall for it, he lops his limbs till they be short enough, and if he be too short, he stretches his limbs till they be long enough: but me only he spared, seven weary years agone; for I alone of all fitted his bed exactly, so he spared me, and made me his slave. And once I was a wealthy merchant, and dwelt in brazen-gated Thebes; but now I hew wood and draw water for him, the torment of all mortal men.’

translation.en: If a man is too tall for it, he chops off his limbs until they are short enough.
translation.kr: 만약 사람이 너무 크면 그는 다리가 짧아질 때까지 잘라냅니다.

translation.en: If he is too short, he stretches his limbs until they are long enough.
translation.kr: 만약 너무 작으면 다리가 길어질 때까지 늘립니다.

translation.en: He only spared me seven weary years ago.
translation.kr: 그는 7년 전 힘들었던 때에 나만을 살려주었습니다.

translation.en: I alone perfectly fitted his bed, so he made me his slave.
translation.kr: 나만이 유일하게 그의 침대에 딱 맞았고 그래서 그는 나를 노예로 삼았습니다.

translation.en: I was once a wealthy merchant living in brazen-gated Thebes.
translation.kr: 저는 한때 청동 문이 있는 테베에 살던 부유한 상인이었습니다.

translation.en: But now I chop wood and draw water for this tormentor of all mortal men.
translation.kr: 하지만 지금은 모든 인간을 괴롭히는 그를 위해 장작을 패고 물을 긷고 있습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus said nothing; but he ground his teeth together.

translation.en: Theseus said nothing, but he ground his teeth together.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 아무 말도 하지 않았지만 이를 갈았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Escape, then,’ said the old man, ‘for he will have no pity on thy youth. But yesterday he brought up hither a young man and a maiden, and fitted them upon his bed; and the young man’s hands and feet he cut off, but the maiden’s limbs he stretched until she died, and so both perished miserably—but I am tired of weeping over the slain.  And therefore he is called Procrustes the stretcher, though his father called him Damastes. Flee from him: yet whither will you flee?  The cliffs are steep, and who can climb them? and there is no other road.’

translation.en: Escape, then, said the old man.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 도망치십시오, 노인이 말했습니다.

translation.en: He will have no pity on your youth.
translation.kr: 그는 당신의 젊음을 불쌍히 여기지 않을 것입니다.

translation.en: Just yesterday he brought a young man and a maiden here.
translation.kr: 바로 어제 그는 젊은 남자와 처녀를 이곳으로 데려왔습니다.

translation.en: He fitted them upon his bed.
translation.kr: 그는 그들을 침대에 맞추었습니다.

translation.en: He cut off the young man's hands and feet.
translation.kr: 그는 젊은 남자의 손과 발을 잘랐습니다.

translation.en: He stretched the maiden's limbs until she died.
translation.kr: 그는 처녀가 죽을 때까지 팔다리를 늘렸습니다.

translation.en: So both perished miserably.
translation.kr: 그래서 두 사람 모두 비참하게 죽고 말았습니다.

translation.en: I am so tired of weeping over the slain.
translation.kr: 살해당한 사람들을 위해 우는 것도 이제 지쳤습니다.

translation.en: That is why he is called Procrustes the stretcher.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 늘리는 자 프로크루스테스라고 불립니다.

translation.en: His father originally named him Damastes.
translation.kr: 그의 아버지는 원래 그를 다마스테스라고 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Flee from him, yet where will you go?
translation.kr: 그에게서 도망치십시오, 하지만 어디로 가시겠습니까?

translation.en: The cliffs are steep, and no one can climb them.
translation.kr: 절벽은 가파르고 아무도 오를 수 없습니다.

translation.en: There is no other road.
translation.kr: 다른 길은 없습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But Theseus laid his hand upon the old man’s month, and said, ‘There is no need to flee;’ and he turned to go down the pass.

translation.en: But Theseus covered the old man's mouth with his hand.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 노인의 입을 손으로 막았습니다.

translation.en: There is no need to flee, he said.
translation.kr: 도망칠 필요가 없습니다, 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: He then turned to head down the pass.
translation.kr: 그러고는 고개를 돌려 길을 따라 내려갔습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
